paper_metadata.title: Microstructure, tensile properties and deformation behaviour of a promising bio-applicable new Ti35Zr15Nb25Ta25 medium entropy alloy (MEA)

evidence.quote: Microstructure, tensile properties and deformation behaviour of a promising bio-applicable new Ti35Zr15Nb25Ta25 medium entropy alloy (MEA)

This research reports a promising bio-applicable new Ti35Zr15Nb25Ta25 (at.%) medium entropy alloy (MEA) designed with an atomic mismatch value (δ) of 4.0% through replacing 10 at.% Zr with 10 at.% Ti in its parent equiatomic TiZrNbTa MEA
This new MEA offers an attractive alternative to Ta, which has found broad applications as bone implants

The Ti35Zr15Nb25Ta25 (at.%) MEA was fabricated from pure elemental nuggets with a minimum purity of 99.95 wt.% using an arc-melting furnace (AM200, Edmund Bühler GmbH) under a titanium-getter pure argon atmosphere. Firstly, five alloy buttons (~20 g) were fabricated. Each alloy button was remelted six times for chemical homogeneity (flipped before each remelting). During each round of melting, the melt was kept in the liquid state for 10 min.
Then all the five buttons were remelted together and cast into a water-cooled copper (Cu) mould to form a cuboidal bar with dimensions of ~90 × 12 × 8 (thickness) mm3.

The as-cast MEA shows a single body centred cubic (BCC) phase with ~81% of its solidification grain boundaries (SGBs) having misorientation angles of > 30°.
Only one BCC phase was detected, with the lattice parameter of 3.331 Å (Table 1), which is nearly identical to that (3.334 Å) estimated using Vegard's law
The uneven contrast (Z-contrast) reflects the difference in composition between the dendrite and inter-dendritic regions due to solidification microsegregation.
The grain size ranges from 40 to 130 μm.
High angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) with misorientation angles (θ) greater than 30° are prominent, accounting for 81.3%.
